A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeNOTS by the same authors. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–B, including equations, figures and tables, are readable and support matching retained, revised and removed material.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark, depth, overfitting and perturbation experiments, including results in Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 reports original benchmark, expressiveness, memory, perturbation and forecasting experiments in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The proposed backbone retains time rescaling, cubic-spline interpolation and GRU(xhat, -h) dynamics with a linear readout. Adaptive and constant feedback become Anti-NF and Sync-NF, while SNCDE names the existing time-scaling construction. These changes do not establish a new DeNOTS algorithm.

E1.justification: V3 retains Sepsis and Pendulum regression, replaces WISDM HAR with U-Wave Gesture Library and InsectSound, and adds Bump classification and SineMix frequency prediction. Appendix B.7 adds Sine-2 and Pendulum-Angles forecasting, including regular and Poisson-sampled observations.

E2.justification: V3 adds TempFormer, Neural RDE and GRU-ODE to the main benchmark and promotes synchronous feedback from an ablation to a main comparator. Forecasting includes Latent ODE. The attack comparison adds Mamba, Neural CDE, Neural RDE and Sync-NF. V2's GRU-based RNN and rotary Transformer match retained GRU and RoFormer comparators.

E3.justification: Sepsis preprocessing changes to zero filling, and its Transformer/Mamba baselines increase from one layer to four/32 layers. Main DeNOTS results use validation-selected depth instead of separately reported fixed depths. V3 introduces tolerance-versus-time-scale sweeps and forecasting masks, and replaces localized HAR attacks with sequence-wide Pendulum corruptions, including replacement by Gaussian noise.

E4.justification: V3 adds tolerance-versus-scaling analyses, weight-norm and feedback-strength diagnostics, a targeted SineMix memory test, and depth-dependent robustness analysis. The small-Pendulum overfitting study is retained but revised in Appendix B.6. V2's attack-offset analysis and fourfold-shortened Pendulum baseline diagnosis are removed. The Gaussian-process Monte Carlo assumption check is retained.

E5.justification: Main benchmarks retain three-run averaging and dispersion reporting already present in v2's appendix. V3 adds Pearson/Spearman summaries and uncertainty-based tie highlighting. Attack reporting changes from ten seeds to five attack seeds across five weight sets, totaling 25 runs per point; feedback-strength plots also disclose five-run variability.

E6.justification: Benchmark entries are extensively revised: Pendulum Neural CDE R2 changes from -0.36 ± 0.16 in v2 Table 4 to 0.76 ± 0.02 in v3 Table 7. V3 adds synthetic-task, forecasting and correlation results, while removing HAR and shortened-Pendulum results. Changed protocols limit direct performance comparisons between versions.

T1.justification: V3 adds the expressiveness theorem and proof, replaces matrix-feedback assumptions with scalar coefficients and f(0)=0, and reformulates stability through an input-to-state Lyapunov argument. It adds cubic-spline error asymptotics, a tightness example and an exponential-kernel shift proof. V2's explicit squared-exponential and minimax bounds are removed, and robustness and forgetfulness derivations are revised.

C1.justification: V3 makes superiority of time scaling over tolerance reduction a central scientific claim and adds a claimed tight cubic-spline risk bound. It recasts forgetfulness from a guaranteed beneficial property into an effect Anti-NF can avoid to preserve long-term memory. These changes go beyond terminology or additional benchmark support.

C2.justification: V3 explains expressiveness through weight norms and memory retention through adaptive weakening of the feedback condition. It adds an accuracy–robustness tradeoff as depth increases and discusses exceptions favoring alternatives in regular forecasting and the Sepsis tolerance ablation. The runtime limitation remains substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds parameter-count tables, fuller MLP/Transformer/Neural RDE implementation descriptions, dataset preparation and licensing information, and hardware and compute estimates in Appendix B.9. It updates the anonymous repository address. Existing solver, optimizer and configuration disclosures largely remain, although the explicit statement disabling batch-normalization affine parameters disappears.

R1.justification: V3 adds a substantial stability discussion covering Lyapunov methods, Stable Neural Flows, constrained ODEs and controlled/rough differential equations, alongside new expressivity and spline references. It removes much of the generic sequence-model survey and positions its stability contribution specifically around externally controlled dynamics.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around NFE, tolerance and time scaling. Separate Time Scaling and Negative Feedback sections interleave theory with experiments, replacing v2's more separated narrative. Terminology and appendix organization change substantially; limitations move into the conclusion and the separate Impact Statement disappears.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive display redesign. V3 adds properties and feedback-comparison tables, replaces the leading depth plot with a log-NFE plot, annotates the method diagram, and replaces the eight-panel HAR attack display with Pendulum plots. Benchmark tables are restructured and uncertainty moves into the main results table.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens evaluation through tolerance-versus-scaling controls, broader comparators, memory diagnostics and resource disclosures. However, its newly central expressiveness guarantee has a substantive flaw: Appendix A.1 uses an invalid product-of-integrals inequality. Under Theorem 3.1's definitions, g(x,h)=x+h, constant inputs 1 and 0, h0=0 and T=1/2 already violate the stated bound. The evaluation improvements coexist with this defect in a main contribution, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
